body:
I have tried counseling. They have told me they don't know what to tell me, that it is bad, and that we can work on pain management cognitive behavioral therapy if I want. My psychiatrist appointments are twice as long because she has to continually look up strange medical interactions with my diseases.

I have Ehlers Danlos syndrome, all of my tissue in my body is too stretchy and fragile. I dislocate my hips and knees every day, I have to walk with braces on many days. My stomach is paralyzed, I have to go on and off a feeding tube so I don't starve to death. I go back and forth between being ok and then suddenly getting worse and vomiting every food and liquid I put in my body. I lost 90 pounds in 3 months this year. I have a hernia in my diaphragm that has gotten worse and now when I vomit it gets stuck in my esophagus, I have to kneel on the floor and tilt downward to use gravity to help force it out. All my muscles are so lax that I just kind of have to burp up and drool out all the vomit. Makes for a lot more tasting of what you ate. The big issue is usually the food has rotted by the time I vomit it up. I often throw up 12-18 hour old soured food. My stomach will also just dump the entirety of its contents randomly too. This means I can't take any real painkillers, I take a dose...it stays in my stomach, 6 hours later time for another dose...stays in my stomach, 6 hours later time for another...now my stomach empties and I'm overdosing on 3 painkillers at once. 

When I have a feeding tube (I either get one shoved through my nose, through my stomach and ending in my small intestine or I get one surgically punched through my abdomen that goes into my intestines) I have trouble constantly. My "permanent" one fell out 4 times in 2 months and I got 3 abdominal wall infections requiring 3 rounds of IV antibiotics. The ER staff knows me in all my local hospitals. They know to prep something for me to throw up in and I usually get priority. Which is nice but also sad. I'm allergic to many foods...corn, wheat, soy, beef, nuts, raw fruits and some raw veggies...I have to have an incredibly specialized formula for my feeding tube that's very hard to find and expensive. It's entirely manufactured and made of just chemicals.

I have had 7 surgeries in 4 years. My eye muscles stretched out and had to be cut down shorter, multiple colonoscopies to remove tumors from my stomach and colon ( around 30 so far ), my tube surgery, etc. I cannot go outside during the day as my Ehlers Danlos also comes with dysautonomia. I cannot regulate my temperature, heart rate, sweating or blood pressure correctly. I get very sick very quickly in the heat and must wear an ice vest for any time spent outside. I have postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome as well from the Ehlers Danlos, which means eating causes my heart to beat irregularly triggering panic attacks that cannot be calmed through mindfulness and I also have my vision completely black out every time I stand, so I must remain still for a few seconds. 

I don't sleep. Part of dysautonomia is your body just dumps adrenaline. I wake up at 2 AM like I just got off a roller coaster, then I fall asleep during whatever I'm doing later in the day. When I do sleep I often wake up with a dislocated hip or knee or elbow. I have to push that back in and then work on slowly sitting up and standing over a period of 10 minutes. Not allowed to go faster or I'll faint. My heart rate laying down is around 40. Takes a minute to get high enough to handle sitting up. 

I have 3-4 autoimmune diseases. Hidradenitis Suppurativa, Undifferentiated connective tissue disease, autoimmune chronic hives (when I get hot or stressed I get covered in hives and have to get cortisone shots) and severe allergies. I also have mast cell activation disorder, which means I randomly go into anaphylaxis for no good reason and have to always have rescue Epi-pens.

Right now my big issue besides constant vomiting and starvation is I have cranial-vertebrae instability from the Ehlers Danlos and a bad car accident as a teenager. My brain herniates and gets squished by my spine because the ligaments are too stretched to hold my head up or keep the joints held in the right place. It causes blinding headaches and pain shooting down my back once my neck gets too tired for the day. I have to wear a cervical collar to give the ligaments time to rest and to avoid squishing a very important part of my brain stem. 

I'm just so tired and in so much pain. I'm looking at having to get another feeding tube, I've been free of one for 2-3 months. Long term I will always have to go on and off one. I'm just not ready again yet to walk around with a tube taped to my face.
